title: Every template encodes a finitely branching omega-tree, uniquely up to local isomorphism, with branches controlled by branches of the template
author: Supakun Panasawatwong; J. K. Truss
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates a template (T*, prec) to finitely branching omega-trees encoded by it: it produces one such tree, shows any two are locally isomorphic, links eventually singleton branches of the template to infinite branches of the tree, and proves that in a suitable finite-support model a template with no eventually singleton branch can encode a tree with no infinite branch at all (statement lines 588-595). The proof constructs the tree level by level while maintaining a bijection between the levels of the template and partitions of the levels of the tree (proof lines 597-608), then argues that the construction's freedom to leave the new points unordered is exactly what produces locally isomorphic but possibly non-isomorphic trees (proof lines 610-614), and finally runs a Fraenkel-Mostowski argument in which the group fixes the template and every would-be infinite branch lives inside a balanced subtree with infinitely many non-singleton entries (proof lines 619-625). The clause that carries the content is the last one, since it is the only place where the absence of choice is used; the first three clauses are a construction and two observations about it. H2.
